meta.scope: Design-side analysis of the checkout service as it stood before the architecture change described in after-architecture.md.

included: checkout and the interfaces it owns
the checkout side of both service dependencies
boundary.security: Session authentication is in scope as an ordinary element; a failure whose agent is an adversary is handed off to threat modeling.

ground_rules: Rows are re-rated only when the update marks them stale.

elements.name: Checkout service
elements.description: Orchestrates pricing, payment authorization, and order persistence for a submitted cart.

elements.name: Payment gateway
elements.description: A third-party card authorization gateway reached over HTTPS.

elements.name: Session authentication
elements.description: The session token issuer and verifier that authenticates a shopper.
elements.security_rationale: Verifies the session token that authenticates a shopper; a wrong accept lets a stranger act as the shopper.

elements.name: Order store
elements.description: The relational store holding orders and their state transitions.

elements.name: Pricing service
elements.description: Returns a priced cart for a shopper and a locale.

functions.statement: Return an authorization decision for a card and an amount within the client's timeout budget
conditions: at or below the per-merchant rate limit

functions.statement: Admit a request only when it carries a session token this component issued and has not expired
conditions: for every request that reaches the checkout interface

functions.statement: Turn a submitted cart into a confirmed order exactly once
Durably persist a confirmed order before acknowledging the write
conditions: across a failover of the store's primary
functions.for_whom: the checkout service and downstream fulfilment

functions.statement: Return a current priced cart for a shopper and a locale

chains.failure_mode: The authorization call exceeds its timeout budget and returns no decision

effects.local: The checkout request abandons the authorization attempt at the timeout.
effects.next_level: Checkout returns a retryable error and the cart is not confirmed.
effects.end: Shoppers cannot complete checkout while the gateway stays degraded.

causes.text: The gateway degrades once promotion traffic passes the per-merchant rate limit

chains.trigger: A promotion drives submissions above the merchant's authorized rate at the gateway

S.rationale: The end effect is loss of checkout for all shoppers while the gateway is degraded, recoverable without data loss.

O.rationale: The trigger is exercised on every promotion and the vulnerable state lasts as long as the promotion window.

D.rationale: The breaker opens on consecutive timeouts and is exercised by an integration suite, so the mode is caught before an operator looks.

chains.failure_mode: A session token is admitted after the moment it should have expired

effects.local: A request is admitted under a session that should have ended.
effects.next_level: Checkout serves a shopper whose session the storefront has already closed.
effects.end: A subset of shoppers keeps an open checkout session longer than the policy allows.

causes.text: The verifier reads the issued-at claim where it should read the expiry claim

controls.description: session token signature verification on every request

S.rationale: The end effect is a policy breach for a subset of shoppers with no loss of access or data.

O.rationale: The vulnerable state exists for every session whose expiry falls inside an open checkout.

D.rationale: The earliest layer that reliably catches the mode is the verifier's unit suite, which covers signatures and not expiry.

chains.failure_mode: A retried submission confirms the same cart twice

effects.local: Two orders are written for one cart.
effects.next_level: The shopper is charged twice and fulfilment ships twice.
effects.end: A subset of shoppers is double-charged until support reverses one order.

causes.text: The idempotency key is scoped to the session rather than to the cart

S.rationale: The end effect is a double charge for a subset of shoppers, reversible by support.

O.rationale: The vulnerable state needs a retry inside one session, which the storefront's backoff makes uncommon.

D.rationale: The contract suite exercises the deduplication path on every build, so a regression is caught before release.

chains.failure_mode: A write is acknowledged to the caller and the order is not durably stored

effects.local: The store returns success for a row that is absent after a failover.
effects.next_level: Checkout confirms an order that fulfilment never receives.
effects.end: Confirmed order data is lost for the affected shoppers.

causes.text: The write path acknowledges before the replica has the row

S.rationale: The end effect is loss of confirmed order data with no recovery path from the store.

O.rationale: The vulnerable state exists only during an unclean failover of the store's primary.

D.rationale: The nightly reconciler catches every dropped row, one day after the loss at worst.

chains.failure_mode: The cart's last quoted price is served after the catalogue price has changed

effects.local: The checkout service prices a cart from a quote that is no longer current.
effects.next_level: The order is confirmed at a price the catalogue no longer offers.
effects.end: A subset of shoppers is charged a stale price and finance carries the correction.

causes.text: The fallback quote has no maximum age

controls.description: cache age dashboard for the last quoted price

S.rationale: The end effect is price staleness for a subset of shoppers, fully recoverable by a correction.

O.rationale: The vulnerable state exists whenever a price change lands during an open session.

D.rationale: The dashboard is watched during price rollouts, which is the earliest layer that reliably shows the mode.
